newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries stymied in London, twos/fives in focus.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries stymied in London, twos/fives in focus.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were little moved in London trade on Tuesday as a dearth of economic news and apprehension about U.S. credit policy kept prices steady.
"We're expecting low volume and lack of interest for the rest of the week," said a dealer at a U.S. bank in London.

The only point of interest, he said, was the $17 billion two-year sale on Tuesday and the $12.5 billion five-year auction on Wednesday. "With no other factors going it should weigh down on the market a little bit," he said.
The long bond at 1032 GMT was around 94-05,07 to yield 7.10 percent versus 94-06 in Tokyo and 94-08 at the New York close.
"Investors really now are sidelined," said Neil Williams, chief economist at Sumitomo Finance International in London.
He said until the payrolls data on May 2 and Federal Open Market Committee meeting on May 20, the market would be muted.
Further out, the market is gearing up for more credit tightening.
"I suggest the Fed is pricing in a lag of around 18 months between any change in short rates and the effect on inflation and on the consumer," Williams said.
But he said the long bond may not fall too far, with yields likely to be capped around 7.50 percent in the months ahead.
"As long as the inflationary numbers are benign the long end can withstand what it can now consider to be a fairly scant tightening," he said.
June T-bonds were at 107-19, down 2/32 from the prior close.
